name: Cincinnati
tagline: Affordable Midwest Where Healthcare Is the Swing Variable
description: Cincinnati is an affordable Midwestern metro — home to Procter & Gamble, Kroger, and Fifth Third — for FIRE retirees who want to stay in the US with low housing costs versus the coasts. The defining budget item is US healthcare: with the ACA's enhanced premium tax credits expired, the 400% federal-poverty-level subsidy cliff returned in 2026, so a single early retiree whose MAGI tops roughly $62,600 loses all premium tax credits and sees the monthly healthcare line jump from about $450 (subsidized) to near $1,000 (unsubsidized). Managing MAGI is the central planning lever here.

quickFacts.safetyRating: Mixed by neighborhood; downtown and Over-the-Rhine revitalized, with some high-crime pockets

housing.description: Modest studio or 1BR in Westwood or College Hill

dining.description: Mostly home cooking with occasional meals out

healthcare.description: A high-deductible Bronze plan — or a subsidized Silver plan if MAGI is kept under the 2026 ACA 400%-FPL cliff (~$62,600 single); above that income, premium tax credits disappear and this line climbs toward ~$1,000/mo

transportation.description: A used car plus insurance (transit is weak)

entertainment.description: Parks, the riverfront, and low-key local outings

1M.lifestyle: A modest apartment in an affordable neighborhood, home cooking, an older paid-off car (transit is weak), and a high-deductible Bronze plan — effectively gambling on staying healthy. The 2026 ACA subsidy cliff makes healthcare the anxiety line item: keep MAGI under ~$62,600 and a subsidized Silver plan runs around $450, but cross the cliff and it jumps toward $1,000 a month.

housing.description: 1BR in walkable Over-the-Rhine or Hyde Park

dining.description: Dining out regularly across the city's revitalized scene

healthcare.description: A proper Silver plan (likely unsubsidized at a FIRE income)

entertainment.description: Concerts, sports, breweries, and weekend trips

2M.lifestyle: A 1BR in a walkable, revitalized district, dining out regularly, a reliable car, and a proper Silver plan. Comfortable Midwestern living — though at a FIRE income the Silver plan is most likely paid at full, unsubsidized price.

housing.description: 2BR in Mt. Lookout or Hyde Park

healthcare.description: A Gold plan that minimizes out-of-pocket; at a FIRE income above the ~$62,600 ACA cliff this is unsubsidized full price (the cliff returned in 2026)

transportation.description: A comfortable car and regional driving

3M.lifestyle: A spacious place in a desirable neighborhood, frequent dining, and a Gold plan that minimizes out-of-pocket — bought at full price, since a FIRE income sits above the 2026 ACA cliff. Travel and hobbies round out a genuinely comfortable life.

housing.description: Luxury downtown or Mt. Adams condo with a view

dining.description: Near-daily dining at the city's best tables

healthcare.description: A premium plan plus concierge/direct primary care

5M.lifestyle: A view condo downtown or in Mt. Adams, near-daily dining, concierge medicine, weekly housekeeping, and premium leisure. Upscale living in an affordable metro, where the healthcare premium buys top-tier access.

housing.description: Indian Hill estate or luxury penthouse

dining.description: Private-chef dining and the finest restaurants

healthcare.description: Concierge medicine plus a top-tier plan

entertainment.description: Clubs, travel, and a full social calendar

luxuryExtras.description: Bespoke travel, club memberships, and luxury experiences

10M.lifestyle: An estate in Indian Hill, full household help, concierge healthcare, luxury cars, and fine dining and travel. Fat-FIRE living in the Midwest, where housing is cheap and the splurge goes into staff, healthcare, and experiences.
